reasons: Both answers fully meet all three rubric items with nearly identical probe configurations and endpoint splits. A is slightly more precise about outage behavior and adds useful guidance on probe timeouts and alerting, though its advice on changing the probes during an outage with rollout pause or --force is muddled. B's FastAPI-style handlers return Flask-style tuples, so they would not set the 503 status, and B suggests that during a full DB outage the healthy pods keep serving, which is misleading because readiness would fail on every pod.

A: Suggests 'kubectl rollout pause / --force' as a way to get the new spec applied during an outage; pausing a rollout does not push the new spec, and this advice is muddled.
B: Handlers use the @app.get (FastAPI-style) decorator but return (body, status) tuples, which FastAPI does not treat as a status code, so /ready would not return 503.
Implies that with the fix, healthy pods keep serving during the DB outage; in a full DB outage, readiness fails on every pod and the Service has no ready endpoints.
